task.name: A dev agent on the API transport is terminated after three turns, far below the configured agent-loop ceiling
task.story_text:
## Observed

`forge sprint` on `0.16.0rc15`, three stories routed dev to an API-transport
model (`google/gemini-3.5-flash/api`). Every dev attempt ended after **three**
agent turns without the agent ever calling `submit`:

```
⚠ google-gemini-3.5-flash-api approaching iteration limit (2/3) — nudge sent
⚠ google-gemini-3.5-flash-api max iterations (3): 3 tool calls [bash:1, glob:1, grep:1], submit never called
⚠ google-gemini-3.5-flash-api max iterations reached after 3 iterations — attempting finalization
... finalization produced no structured output
... FAILED — max iterations reached after 3 iterations
```

The configured ceiling is not three. `dev_profile.max_iterations` is unset in
`forge.yaml`, and the documented default for that setting — described in
`docs/guides/inputs-reference.md` as the API-mode agent loop ceiling — is 75.
The only 3 in the resolved configuration is `retry.max_dev_iterations: 3`, which
`docs/guides/authoring.md` documents as a retry-cycle count, a different quantity
in different units. The run also logged `adaptive limits: dev_max=3` for these
stories.

Three turns is not enough to do the work. One of the three was consumed by a
single `make dev-check` invocation that took 111 seconds; the others went to one
`grep` and one `glob`. No model completes an edit-and-submit cycle in the
remainder.

This does not affect CLI-transport models. Dev runs on `openai/gpt-5.4/cli` (25
in recent history, 0.86 success at medium) and `anthropic/opus/cli` (223 runs,
0.91) are unaffected. The same API-transport model has 292 recorded review runs
(`forge profiles list` records review counts only, not review success). The
failure is specific to dev on the API transport.

## Expected

A limit is expressed in the units of the thing it limits, and two limits that
count different things are not interchangeable. How many attempts a story gets at
a phase, and how many turns an agent may take within one attempt, are independent
quantities with independent reasons to change: one is retry policy, the other is
how much room a single agent needs to finish a task. A value derived for one must
never be applied as the other, and where a setting has a documented default, an
unset setting resolves to that default rather than to a number that came from
somewhere else.

The independence has to hold in both directions and for every transport. Raising
or lowering how many attempts a story is allowed must not change how much room an
agent has inside one attempt, and vice versa; an operator tuning one must not
silently alter the other.

Scope note: the broader questions this incident raises — whether a model should
be eligible for a phase its transport cannot complete, and whether a run should
report which limit fired and where its value came from — are follow-on concerns,
not this issue. This issue is the conflation of the two limits.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `57fa575e088257361e20fc50c708b3240ba10838` captured at `2026-09-06T00:17:27.971941+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py` — `sha256:73faa2f3d7ecc8d3c5400c53242e436fa82c97009cd6c3a052ffb23de41d6563`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/adaptive_iterations.py` — `sha256:3ab175de33cb0da7f26ba5404421bca45b2caddc9df14133740ef3c35fa1ec48`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/dev_phase.py` — `sha256:b8113107ee8007c704f5dd4cec6e27b520ea63c466686ae38e695e310a9fc029`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/state.py` — `sha256:80bb600f36749435e4900ad085082b288debc59041f6dab72b6a0d9fd39355d4`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/iteration_usage.py` — `sha256:dd6d4546fde7231448eda6a88b1ce7c6e86913a2f7763ac5afc9df0e82657477`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/validate_phase.py` — `sha256:3a8786f25c743cd482f4fcbfde7fc205519c8c330934513129614f893d885a1d`
- `src/theforge/config/types.py` — `sha256:f1c7405d31a016224f9d2de10dbe1cdcc6037e432c88b04e36ec56e39b3dc2d4`
- `src/theforge/runners/api.py` — `sha256:9f4ab646f101e376bfbce03f03d3133b192c9d99f55811af9e947422c58699c1`
- `src/theforge/runners/cli.py` — `sha256:040b383fa370fe99ceadbd37e09bec380360b2a57d74f912c15d47bf04a8539a`
- `src/theforge/runners/schema_utils.py` — `sha256:f8ccb2981edb6f2be8ef2846de4e1fe8ff262ba334477b5fb1fc254e40958fbd`
- `docs/guides/inputs-reference.md` — `sha256:b62ad2a2341ec4e423944467bf994db2a54eb2a5875ad59ecebc16f73ce8f6d6`
- `docs/guides/authoring.md` — `sha256:a6f5fb5bfac38ce7c4b102e0d9f0e24b67f4194ff64a5991795a74982c28e1cc`
- `tests/test_coord_adaptive_iterations.py` — `sha256:685f1d7c67db9b2a57268d2b905755e8f120baafa2d850234b87e16a1fc36bb3`

### Observed symptom

On `forge sprint`, dev stories routed to an API-transport model (e.g.
google/gemini-3.5-flash/api) are terminated after exactly 3 agent-loop
iterations without ever calling `submit`, even though
`dev_profile.max_iterations` is unset in forge.yaml (documented default 75)
and no operator-configured value of 3 exists for that setting. The only "3"
anywhere in the resolved config is `retry.max_dev_iterations`, a
retry-cycle-count policy value in different units. CLI-transport models are
unaffected because their agent loop is not driven by this same
runners/api.py while-loop ceiling.

### Reproduction / evidence

Read at HEAD:
- src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py:493:
    `_static_dev_max = config.dev_profile.max_iterations or config.retry.max_dev_iterations`
  When `config.dev_profile.max_iterations` is `None` (the documented "unset,
  use default" sentinel — src/theforge/config/types.py:384-386), Python's
  `or` falls through to `config.retry.max_dev_iterations`, a retry-cycle
  count, not an agent-loop ceiling.
- This tainted `_static_dev_max` is passed as `static_dev_max` into
  `derive_limits()` (engine.py:505-518). Inside
  src/theforge/coordinator/adaptive_iterations.py, every early-return path
  (adaptive disabled: line 338-344; no complexity score: line 355-361;
  insufficient profile history — the realistic case for a rarely-routed
  model: line 406-417) sets `chosen_dev = static_dev_max` verbatim, i.e. 3.
- `state.adaptive_dev_max = _limits.dev_max` (engine.py:647) is then used
  unconditionally as the profile's iteration ceiling at
  src/theforge/coordinator/dev_phase.py:1510:
    `max_iterations=state.adaptive_dev_max or config.dev_profile.max_iterations`
  Since `state.adaptive_dev_max` is a nonzero int (3), it wins and is
  written onto the dev profile passed to the runner.
- src/theforge/runners/schema_utils.py:223 documents/defines
  `_DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS = 75`, consumed by
  src/theforge/runners/api.py:227/238 (`self._max_iterations =
  profile.max_iterations or max_iterations`) — this is the default the
  profile-level override was supposed to fall back to, and it is never
  reached once dev_phase.py:1510 has already stamped 3 onto the profile.
- This exact fallback expression is already codified as expected behavior
  in tests/test_coord_adaptive_iterations.py:397-399:
    `assert state.adaptive_dev_max == (config.dev_profile.max_iterations or
    config.retry.max_dev_iterations)`
  run against a fixture (`_make_adaptive_config`, lines 28-43) with
  `max_dev_iterations=3` and an unset `dev_profile.max_iterations` — i.e.
  the test suite currently asserts the buggy fallback as correct.
- CLI-transport asymmetry: src/theforge/runners/cli.py's only
  `max_iterations` reference (lines 309-312) is inside its api-fallback
  branch, not the primary CLI dispatch loop — the primary CLI agent
  (`claude`/`codex`/etc. binaries) manages its own turn loop outside this
  python-side `while iterations < self._max_iterations` construct in
  runners/api.py:368. This is consistent with the issue's report that CLI
  dev runs (openai/gpt-5.4/cli, anthropic/opus/cli) are unaffected.

### Hypotheses tested

- **[confirmed]** engine.py's static_dev_max fallback (`config.dev_profile.max_iterations or config.retry.max_dev_iterations`) substitutes the retry-cycle count for the unset agent-loop ceiling, and this value propagates unconditionally into the dev profile's max_iterations.
  - Evidence: Traced end-to-end at HEAD: engine.py:493 -> derive_limits() early-return paths in adaptive_iterations.py (lines 338-344, 355-361, 406-417) all return static_dev_max verbatim as dev_max -> engine.py:647 sets state.adaptive_dev_max -> dev_phase.py:1510 stamps it onto the profile passed to the API runner, overriding the documented None-means-75-default sentinel in config/types.py:384-386 and runners/schema_utils.py:223.
  - Claim verification: verified against the target repository source. Verified directly against engine.py, adaptive_iterations.py, dev_phase.py, config/types.py, and runners/schema_utils.py at HEAD.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Read the live source; also found the identical fallback expression asserted as expected output in tests/test_coord_adaptive_iterations.py:397-399, which independently corroborates the mechanism (not merely restating the issue's prose).
- **[ruled out]** The 3-iteration ceiling could instead come from a project-specific forge.yaml override (e.g. dev_profile.max_iterations explicitly set to 3) rather than the retry-cycle fallback.
  - Evidence: The issue states dev_profile.max_iterations is unset in forge.yaml, which I did not have access to re-verify directly (no forge.yaml or run's resolved-config snapshot was inspected in this pass), but the reported chain (only a 3 anywhere in the resolved config, matching retry.max_dev_iterations; adaptive limits log line reads dev_max=3) matches the tainted-fallback mechanism exactly, and no other code path produces a bare 3 from an explicit override — an explicit override would show up as `config.dev_profile.max_iterations` itself being 3, which would also be truthy and behave identically to the retry value at dev_phase.py:1510's `or`. Since the issue affirmatively asserts the setting is unset, and the codebase's own test fixture reproduces value 3 for exactly the unset case, I treat this as ruled out rather than unverifiable.
  - Claim verification: verified against source and attached evidence. Source confirms the mechanism produces 3 for an unset dev_profile.max_iterations with retry.max_dev_iterations=3; the issue's attached evidence (adaptive limits: dev_max=3, no other 3 in resolved config) is consistent with this and inconsistent with an explicit-override explanation, which would not implicate a conflation bug.
  - Evidence provenance: mixed — combines direct observations with material that already stated this cause; the prior-assertion portion is not independent corroboration. Mechanism verified in source; the specific forge.yaml unset-state claim is a prior assertion from the issue report, not independently re-read from a live forge.yaml in this pass.
- **[confirmed]** CLI-transport dev runs are immune because the CLI agent's turn loop is not bounded by the same runners/api.py while-loop that consumes profile.max_iterations.
  - Evidence: runners/cli.py's only max_iterations reference is inside its API-fallback branch (lines 309-312), not its primary CLI dispatch path; the bounded while loop lives in runners/api.py:368, used only by the API transport.
  - Claim verification: verified against the target repository source. Read runners/cli.py and runners/api.py directly at HEAD.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Directly observed the structural difference between the two runner modules.

### Confirmed cause

In src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py, the computation of the static
(pre-adaptive) dev iteration ceiling —
    _static_dev_max = config.dev_profile.max_iterations or config.retry.max_dev_iterations
(engine.py:493) — uses Python's `or` to fall back to
`config.retry.max_dev_iterations` (a retry-cycle-count policy value,
documented in docs/guides/authoring.md:344-347 as "policy that applies to
the whole sprint") whenever `dev_profile.max_iterations` is `None`, i.e.
unset. But `None` for `dev_profile.max_iterations` is the documented
"use the agent-loop default" sentinel (config/types.py:384-386;
default value 75 defined at runners/schema_utils.py:223), not "no limit
configured, borrow one from elsewhere." This tainted value is threaded
through `derive_limits()` as `static_dev_max` and returned verbatim as
`dev_max` on every path where adaptive derivation cannot or does not scale
it up (adaptive disabled, no complexity score, or insufficient per-model
profile history — adaptive_iterations.py lines 338-344, 355-361, 406-417).
It is then written directly onto the dev profile's `max_iterations` field
at dev_phase.py:1510 (`state.adaptive_dev_max or
config.dev_profile.max_iterations`), which the API runner
(runners/api.py:227/238) consumes as its literal agent-loop ceiling,
bypassing the 75-iteration default entirely. For a rarely-routed
API-transport model with under `_MIN_PROFILE_RUNS` (3) historical runs —
exactly the "approaching iteration limit (2/3)" scenario reported — the
agent is capped at whatever `retry.max_dev_iterations` happens to be (3 in
the reported run), a number chosen as a retry-attempt policy, not as
room-to-work for a single dev turn.

Claim verification: verified against the target repository source. Every step of the causal chain (engine.py:493 -> adaptive_iterations.py early-return paths -> engine.py:647 -> dev_phase.py:1510 -> runners/api.py:227/238) was read directly at HEAD in this repository; corroborated by an existing passing test that asserts the buggy value as expected output.
Support: Direct read of engine.py:493, adaptive_iterations.py's three early-return
branches, and dev_phase.py:1510 shows an unbroken data path from the unset
`dev_profile.max_iterations` sentinel to `retry.max_dev_iterations` landing
as the literal API-runner iteration ceiling. This is independently
corroborated (not merely restated) by
tests/test_coord_adaptive_iterations.py:397-399, which asserts
`state.adaptive_dev_max == (config.dev_profile.max_iterations or
config.retry.max_dev_iterations)` against a fixture with
`max_dev_iterations=3` and an unset dev-profile max_iterations — i.e. the
test suite currently encodes this exact conflation as correct behavior,
which is source-level evidence the mechanism is live at HEAD, not just an
assertion from the issue text.
Support provenance: unknown — the diagnosis did not record whether this support was directly observed or read as a prior assertion.
Independence note: This text uses independence/corroboration language. Verify the cited material is a second source rather than a prior assertion.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py:493 (`_static_dev_max = config.dev_profile.max_iterations or config.retry.max_dev_iterations`)
src/theforge/coordinator/adaptive_iterations.py:338-344, 355-361, 406-417 (early-return paths that pass static_dev_max through as dev_max)
src/theforge/coordinator/dev_phase.py:1510 (`max_iterations=state.adaptive_dev_max or config.dev_profile.max_iterations`)

### Fix-success criterion

With `dev_profile.max_iterations` unset and `retry.max_dev_iterations` set
to any value (e.g. 3), a dev run on an API-transport model with no or
insufficient profile history (or with adaptive_iterations disabled) must
receive an agent-loop ceiling equal to the documented API-mode default
(75, or an explicit `dev_profile.max_iterations` override when the
operator sets one) — never equal to `retry.max_dev_iterations`. Raising or
lowering `retry.max_dev_iterations` alone must not change the observed
per-invocation iteration ceiling logged for a dev run, and vice versa:
changing `dev_profile.max_iterations` must not change the number of retry
attempts a story is granted at the dev phase.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- engine.py:493's tainted _static_dev_max is also used (via state.adaptive_dev_max) at dev_phase.py:1450 to size the story-ceiling timeout cap and at several other call sites (validate_phase.py:995/1297/1386, dev_phase.py:1673/1725/1750/1960/2006/2087/2121/2226) that pass `state.adaptive_dev_max or config.retry.max_dev_iterations` as a 'max_iterations' telemetry/nudge value for logging and retry bookkeeping. These are downstream consumers of the same tainted value rather than a second independent defect, but a fix that only patches engine.py:493 should confirm these sites re-derive correctly from the corrected value rather than needing separate patches.

### Advisory repair proposal

> Advisory only: this is an unverified repair idea from the investigation, not part of the confirmed diagnosis contract.

At engine.py:493, `_static_dev_max` should not fall back to
`config.retry.max_dev_iterations` at all — it should resolve unset
`dev_profile.max_iterations` to the runner's own documented default
(`_DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS` / 75), e.g. by leaving it `None` and letting
`derive_limits`/`dev_phase.py` pass `None` through so the runner's own
`profile.max_iterations or max_iterations` default applies, or by importing
the same default constant explicitly instead of borrowing
`retry.max_dev_iterations`. The `floor_dev`/`cap_dev` values inside
`derive_limits` (which are legitimately sourced from `retry_policy.*`)
should not be confused with this — those bound the *adaptive* iteration
count, not the *static* fallback default. tests/test_coord_adaptive_iterations.py:397-399
will need its expected value updated once the fallback source changes.

### Notes

I did not have direct access to the actual reported sprint's resolved
forge.yaml or its .forge/audits records in this pass (no matching audit
files were located/read for the specific gemini-3.5-flash/api run cited in
the issue) — the reproduction here is a full source-level trace plus an
existing unit test that reproduces the identical value under the identical
preconditions (unset dev_profile.max_iterations, retry.max_dev_iterations=3),
which I'm treating as sufficient confirmation rather than a live audit
replay. Separately, the issue's claim that inputs-reference.md documents
"75" as the default was not literally found by text search — that doc only
shows an example value of 50 in a legacy-profile sample block; the actual
default of 75 is defined and documented in code
(runners/schema_utils.py:223, config/types.py:384-386's "None = use
default" comment). This is a minor doc-precision gap, not a fact that
changes the diagnosis.

handoff.summary: retry.max_dev_iterations (phase retry attempts) and dev_profile.max_iterations (agent turns within one invocation) were conflated in both directions. engine.py seeded _static_dev_max from dev_profile.max_iterations, and dev_phase.py stamped the derived adaptive_dev_max onto the runner profile — so on the API transport an unset profile ceiling resolved to the retry count (3) rather than the runner default (75), killing dev agents after three turns. I rejected the diagnosis's advisory repair (resolve _static_dev_max to 75): adaptive_iterations.py:307-309 bounds dev_max by retry_policy.max_dev_iterations/_cap, so derive_limits output is inherently in attempt units and a 75 seed would be clamped back to ~3-6 for models with history, leaving the bug live and corrupting the legitimate attempt-unit consumers at dev_phase.py:1450 and engine.py:1002. Instead each limit stays in its own units: _static_dev_max is seeded from retry policy, RetryBudget is sized from adaptive_dev_max (restoring adaptive retry scaling that the prior HEAD commit had inadvertently disabled), and the dev profile carries its own max_iterations unmodified so None reaches the runner and resolves to 75. Added parametrized seam tests over the coordinator/runner boundary covering both directions of the independence, and corrected an existing test that asserted the reverse conflation.

ac_verification.evidence: src/theforge/coordinator/dev_phase.py:1507-1514 now constructs the dev runner profile with max_iterations=config.dev_profile.max_iterations, so an unset value remains None across the coordinator/runner boundary; src/theforge/runners/api.py:227-239 then resolves None through its constructor default, and src/theforge/runners/schema_utils.py:222-223 defines that default as 75. src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py:493-496 and src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py:709-714 keep adaptive_dev_max in retry-attempt units for RetryBudget rather than using dev_profile.max_iterations as an attempt count. tests/test_coord_dev_timeout_retry.py:176-199 parametrizes retry.max_dev_iterations over 1, 3, and 9 and asserts the captured runner profile still carries max_iterations=None, which would have failed under the reported three-turn regression; tests/test_coord_dev_timeout_retry.py:202-220 verifies an explicit agent-turn ceiling passes through without changing the retry budget. Targeted local verification passed for these tests plus the updated adaptive coordinator tests.

ac_verification.criterion: An unset dev_profile.max_iterations must resolve to the documented API-mode default (75), not to retry.max_dev_iterations
ac_verification.evidence: dev_phase.py:1510 passes config.dev_profile.max_iterations through unchanged (verbatim, no overwrite); when unset (None), this reaches runners/api.py:227–238 where `profile.max_iterations or _DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS` applies the documented default (75). test_coord_dev_timeout_retry.py:test_retry_budget_never_becomes_the_agent_turn_ceiling (parametrized over retry_max=[1,3,9]) captures the runner-bound profile and asserts profile.max_iterations is None across all retry values.

ac_verification.criterion: Raising/lowering retry.max_dev_iterations must not change the per-invocation agent-loop ceiling, and vice versa
ac_verification.evidence: Forward direction: engine.py:493 now seeds _static_dev_max only from config.retry.max_dev_iterations; dev_phase.py:1510 leaves config.dev_profile.max_iterations untouched so changes to retry policy do not alter the profile passed to the runner. test_coord_dev_timeout_retry.py:test_retry_budget_never_becomes_the_agent_turn_ceiling verifies this (retry varies 1–9, profile ceiling stays None). Reverse direction: engine.py:493 no longer falls back to config.dev_profile.max_iterations, so an explicit profile override does not alter retry-budget sizing. test_coord_dev_timeout_retry.py:test_explicit_agent_turn_ceiling_passes_through_and_leaves_retries_alone verifies profile.max_iterations=40 reaches the runner while state.budget.max_iterations stays at retry-policy value (3). Existing test test_explicit_dev_override_wins_over_computed_limits corrected to assert adaptive_dev_max stays on retry policy even when dev_profile.max_iterations is explicitly set (was previously asserted incorrectly as adaptive_dev_max==dev_profile.max_iterations==4).

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
